blocks.text: Then the students asked the Teacher: "Who is the unseen Friend standing in the chariot beside the soul?"
The Teacher answered their question this way:

"Inside every living soul, there is a quiet Light that comes from neither the body nor the mind. This is Him. He sits in the heart of every being, like an unseen Companion. The Voice we sometimes hear belongs to Him, and it always knows the right way through the battlefield.

He is not a thought, not a feeling, not the voice of the mind. But He whispers through our thoughts, guides through our senses, teaches through events. He is closer than your breath, and deeper than your memory. He lives in every atom, and beside every soul."
The Teacher said that one single Force moves both atoms and stars. The one who fills the whole Universe also fills your heart.

His Spark is in every atom. His light is in every ray. His presence can be heard in every bit of space. He is energy and the source of energy, form and the absence of form, meaning and the emptiness of meaning.
He Is the Root of All Elements
The Great Teacher said that the earth holds together through his patience, water flows from his softness, fire burns by his will, wind moves from his freedom, and space expands from his endlessness.
He is not just the creator — he is the very principle of creation itself. He is the source of all elements and of time's movement. Everything seen and unseen is, at its core, his breath.
He is both the map and the road.
His Name Is a Mystery
The Teacher said his Name is a mystery, just as He is. People call him by many names.

Theologians call him God. Agnostics call him the Universal Mind. The wise call him the Source of Everything. Yogis call him the Oversoul. Buddhists call him Buddha. Taoists call him Tao. Sensitive souls and poets call him Love.
He is beyond every name, and at the same time, inside every name. But a Name is a bridge that can lead you to Him.
He is the twofold Being behind everything. Inside him are both the masculine and the feminine. Softness and strength, silence and action, emptiness and fullness, light and shadow, wisdom and play.
He is not split into opposites. He is the wholeness from which all opposites grow.
He knows everything — and yet he still comes to know himself.
The Teacher said He knows everything about the seen and unseen world. But He is infinite, so He comes to know himself through his own creations.

Through the movement of stars, He learns order. Through the lives of people, He learns love. Through suffering, He learns compassion. Through joy, He learns fullness. Through silence, He learns depth.
He comes to know himself through us, and we come to know ourselves through him.
You can search for Him in a thousand ways. But only love leads you to truly know his nature.
When someone wakes up from the games of worldly life, they start searching for Him. But once they find Him, they understand: this meeting is only the beginning.
You can search for Him through wisdom, through discipline, through service, through looking inside yourself, through watching nature, and through clean, honest actions.
But all these paths are just preparation for one thing. Every river flows into the same Ocean of love.
The Teacher said the highest knowledge doesn't live in the mind. It lives in the heart.
Wisdom can point the way. But only love can help you walk it.

You cannot force your way to knowing Him — not through understanding, not through hard work, not through books. But you can meet Him with an open, honest heart — a heart that recognizes Him as its true home.
The path to Him never ends.
Whoever searches for Him keeps walking. And whoever finds Him keeps walking too.

He is not a destination — He is the heart's endless path. The seeker and the one who has found Him are just two sides of the same traveler. This path is called the Path of Love — the path of friendship with the one who made the world. This is Bhakti-yoga: the yoga of the heart, the yoga of union, the journey home to the one who was always there. The eternal Friend, standing beside the soul in its chariot, waiting for it to turn around.
